title: Product-projection localization and the QAC0 parity lower bound
summary: We prove that constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage using polynomially many qubits. Ancillas start in zero, only one output qubit is measured, and all final garbage is unrestricted. This resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model.

review.reason: Shows constant-depth quantum circuits cannot compute parity with fixed advantage using polynomial qubits.
